Governor Dikko Radda of Katsina State has directed the immediate payment of all outstanding entitlements due to traditional rulers across the state.
Radda gave the directive on Saturday during an engagement with traditional rulers, religious leaders and community representatives at the palace of the District Head of Baure.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the engagement was part of the Tinubu/Dikko/Jobe campaign tour of Daura Zone.
He said no traditional titleholder entitled to such payments should be neglected, urging those experiencing delays to report directly to his office with relevant details for prompt intervention.
“I regard you as my parents, and I am your son. I am here to pay my respects and appreciate your prayers, guidance and support,” he said.
The governor also pledged to contribute from his personal resources towards the renovation of an uncompleted Mosque in the area following an appeal by community stakeholders.
He recalled that Baure was among the communities where his campaign began in 2023, saying his return was to fulfil his promise to appreciate the people for their support.
Radda commended the residents for their peaceful reception and reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to collaborating with traditional rulers, religious leaders and communities to address insecurity, promote peaceful coexistence and accelerate development.
He explained that the Community Development Programme (CDP) initiative was introduced to enable communities to identify and prioritise projects according to their needs.
The governor also acknowledged the contributions of the late President Muhammadu Buhari, assuring that his administration would sustain his legacy while improving the welfare of residents. (NAN)
